questions.stem: A microbiologist samples decaying leaf litter from a forest floor and isolates a filamentous fungus that grows readily on the dead plant material. Most fungi obtain their energy in which of the following ways?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absorption of nutrients from decomposing organic matter

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fixation of atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia for biosynthesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obligate intracellular replication within living host cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxidation of inorganic sulfur compounds present in the soil

choices.label: E
choices.text: Photosynthesis using chlorophyll contained within the hyphae

explanation.summary: Most fungi are saprophytes that feed on decomposing dead organic material.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fungi are eukaryotic organisms that obtain energy from other animals and plants. The majority are saprophytes, meaning they feed on decomposing, dead organic material, which is why they are essential in ecosystems for turning over organic matter. Like bacteria, most fungi are harmless or even helpful to humans.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Nitrogen fixation is a bacterial capability and is not how fungi meet their energy needs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fungi are not obligate intracellular organisms; most live freely in soil and decaying matter.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxidizing inorganic sulfur is a bacterial lifestyle; fungi digest organic material instead.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fungi contain no chlorophyll and do not photosynthesize; they take their energy from other organisms.

questions.stem: A student examining stained fungal hyphae under the microscope sees regularly spaced cross-walls that divide each filament into segments. Which of the following best describes these structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attachment organelles that anchor the mycelium to the substrate surface

choices.label: B
choices.text: Breaks in the hyphae that let macromolecules and organelles pass between segments

choices.label: C
choices.text: Membrane pores through which ergosterol is exported to the cell wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rigid plugs that permanently isolate each hyphal segment from its neighbors

choices.label: E
choices.text: Specialized sites where conidia are assembled before release into the air

explanation.summary: Septa are breaks within hyphae that allow macromolecules and even organelles to flow between hyphal segments.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hyphae may contain septa, which are breaks throughout the hyphae that allow macromolecules and even organelles to flow between hyphal segments. Some fungi do not have septa at all, so the presence or absence of septa is one useful way to tell fungi apart in the laboratory.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Septa have no anchoring role; hyphae themselves extend into the substrate for nutrients.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Septa are structural breaks in the hyphae, not transport pores for sterols.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Septa do not seal segments off; material moves across them between hyphal compartments.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Conidia are produced by spore-producing structures, not by the septa within a hypha.

questions.stem: A fungal colony is spreading outward across an agar plate through branching filamentous structures. These structures serve which of the following primary functions for the colony?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Converting host cholesterol into ergosterol for membrane synthesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fixing carbon dioxide into sugars distributed through the mycelium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Producing antibodies that neutralize competing bacterial species

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reaching into the environment and secreting enzymes that digest nutrients

choices.label: E
choices.text: Storing dormant conidia until ambient temperature reaches 37°C

explanation.summary: Hyphae extend into the environment to find nutrients, then secrete enzymes that break those nutrients down for absorption.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fungi live in colonies called mycelia that are connected by vegetative hyphae, which are branching filamentous structures. Hyphae reach out into the environment for nutrients to absorb and secrete enzymes that break those nutrients down for easier digestion. Hyphae also participate in fungal sexual reproduction by fusing with one another.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fungi synthesize their own ergosterol and do not depend on converting host cholesterol.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Carbon fixation is a plant and cyanobacterial process; fungi absorb preformed organic nutrients.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fungi do not make antibodies; antibody production is a function of the host adaptive immune system.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Conidia break off and disperse rather than being warehoused in hyphae until a temperature threshold.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus undergoes debridement of a necrotic sinus lesion. Histologic sections of the tissue show broad, branching hyphae that contain no cross-walls. Which of the following organisms is most consistent with these findings?

explanation.summary: Mucor spp. are opportunistic fungi whose hyphae are aseptate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both Mucor spp. and Aspergillus spp. are opportunist fungi that cause severe disease in immunocompromised hosts, and they are distinguished on histology by their hyphae. Mucor spp. have aseptate hyphae, meaning the filaments lack the cross-walls seen in other molds. Finding branching hyphae without septa therefore points to Mucor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. have septate hyphae, so visible cross-walls would be expected in the tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces dermatitidis appears in tissue as a thick-walled budding yeast rather than as hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Candida albicans is a dimorphic organism that is a component of normal flora, not an aseptate mold in tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Histoplasma capsulatum appears in tissue as a budding yeast, not as broad aseptate hyphae.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman receiving induction chemotherapy for leukemia develops fever and a cavitary lung lesion. Lung biopsy shows branching filamentous hyphae that are divided at regular intervals by cross-walls. Which of the following organisms is most consistent with these findings?

explanation.summary: Aspergillus spp. are opportunistic fungi with septate hyphae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aspergillus spp. are opportunistic fungi that cause severe disease in the immunocompromised, and their hyphae are septate. The cross-walls seen in this biopsy are the septa that distinguish Aspergillus from the aseptate molds. Presence or absence of septa is a key morphologic discriminator between these look-alike opportunists.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces dermatitidis appears in tissue as a broad-based budding yeast, not as hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptococcus spp. are exogenous yeasts rather than septate molds in tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Histoplasma capsulatum is seen in tissue as a small budding yeast, not as septate hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mucor spp. have aseptate hyphae, so the regular cross-walls described here argue against it.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role that conidia play in fungal biology?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They anchor the mycelium to decomposing organic substrate

choices.label: B
choices.text: They form the rigid outer layer of the fungal cell wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: They fuse with a second hypha to create a binucleated cell

choices.label: D
choices.text: They secrete keratinase to digest the stratum corneum

choices.label: E
choices.text: They travel through air and water to establish new colonies

explanation.summary: Conidia are fungal spores that break off the mycelium and disperse through air and water to found new colonies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Conidia can break off from the mycelium and use air and water to travel to new locations and start a new fungal colony, which is a critical way fungi spread. In human infection, we either inhale these conidia or have them land on our skin. Because bacteria also form spores, fungal spores are given the separate name conidia to minimize confusion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anchoring and nutrient absorption in the substrate are functions of the vegetative hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The rigid outer layer of the fungal cell is the cell wall built of β-glucans and chitin, not conidia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fusion of two hyphae to form a binucleated cell is plasmogamy, a function of hyphae rather than conidia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Keratinase production is a property of dermatophytes invading skin, not a general role of conidia.

questions.stem: A mycology laboratory is characterizing the spores released from a mold colony. Fungal conidia are best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Binucleated cells produced immediately after cytoplasmic fusion occurs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diploid cells that are metabolically active and require enriched media

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dormant bacterial endospores acquired from contaminating normal flora

choices.label: D
choices.text: Haploid cells with few metabolic demands that withstand tough environments

choices.label: E
choices.text: Multinucleate hyphal fragments that have shed their surrounding cell wall

explanation.summary: Conidia are specialized haploid cells optimized for transport: mobile, metabolically undemanding, and hardy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fungal spores are specialized haploid cells optimized for transportation. They are mobile, have few metabolic demands, and are able to withstand tough environments, which is what makes them effective vehicles for spreading a fungus to new locations. These fungal spores are termed conidia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A binucleated cell arises from plasmogamy between hyphae, which is a separate step from conidium formation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Conidia are haploid and metabolically undemanding rather than diploid and nutritionally fastidious.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Conidia are fungal, not bacterial; the separate name exists precisely to avoid confusion with bacterial spores.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Conidia are discrete walled cells, not wall-less fragments broken off from a hypha.

questions.stem: A soil isolate is grown at 25°C and stained with lactophenol blue. Microscopy of the mold shows both small conidia and distinctly large conidia that have a sun-like appearance. Which of the following organisms is most consistent with this finding?

explanation.summary: Histoplasma capsulatum makes both microconidia and macroconidia, and its macroconidia have a distinctive large, sun-like appearance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Conidia can be small (microconidia) or large (macroconidia), and a given fungus may produce one type or both. Histoplasma capsulatum possesses both microconidia and macroconidia, and its macroconidia are distinct, with a large, sun-like appearance. The type and appearance of conidia is one of the features used to distinguish fungi in the laboratory.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. are recognized by septate hyphae rather than by large sun-like macroconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces dermatitidis possesses only microconidia, so large sun-like macroconidia would not be seen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Candida albicans grows as a budding yeast whose form depends on nutrients and pH, not as a conidia-bearing mold.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mucor spp. are identified by their aseptate hyphae, not by a pair of distinctive conidial sizes.

questions.stem: A thermally dimorphic fungus isolated from a patient's respiratory specimen is grown at room temperature. Microscopy of the mold phase shows only small conidia; no large conidia are present. Which of the following organisms best fits this finding?

explanation.summary: Blastomyces dermatitidis possesses only microconidia, which separates it from Histoplasma capsulatum.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blastomyces dermatitidis and Histoplasma capsulatum are both thermally dimorphic and can be told apart by their conidia. Blastomyces dermatitidis possesses only microconidia, whereas Histoplasma capsulatum possesses both microconidia and macroconidia. Finding small conidia alone in the mold phase therefore favors Blastomyces.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Candida albicans is dimorphic on the basis of nutrients and pH, not temperature, and is not a conidia-forming mold.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptococcus spp. are exogenous yeasts and are not among the thermally dimorphic conidia-formers described here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Histoplasma capsulatum would also show its distinctive large, sun-like macroconidia alongside the microconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mucor spp. are not thermally dimorphic and are identified by their aseptate hyphae.

questions.stem: During sexual reproduction in fungi, cells from two genetically independent hyphae fuse so that the resulting single cell contains one nucleus from each parent hypha. This step is called which of the following?

explanation.summary: Plasmogamy is the fusion of cytoplasm from two hyphae, creating a binucleated (dikaryotic) cell.
explanation.whyCorrect: In fungal sexual reproduction, cells from two different hyphae fuse to form a binucleated cell in a step called plasmogamy, with one nucleus contributed by each genetically independent hypha. The cell at this point is dikaryotic (n + n) because the two nuclei have not yet merged.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Budding is a mode of asexual division in yeasts and involves only one parent cell.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Germination is the later process in which dispersed conidia form new mycelia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Karyogamy is fusion of the two nuclei into a diploid zygote, which follows plasmogamy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Meiosis occurs after nuclear fusion and generates the conidia that are subsequently dispersed.

questions.stem: Two fungal hyphae have fused, and the resulting cell is now dikaryotic (n + n). Which of the following events occurs next, and what is its immediate product?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Budding, producing a haploid (n) daughter yeast

choices.label: B
choices.text: Germination, producing a binucleated (n + n) conidium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Meiosis, producing a dikaryotic (n + n) hypha

explanation.summary: After plasmogamy creates a dikaryotic cell, karyogamy fuses the two nuclei into a diploid zygote.
explanation.whyCorrect: Plasmogamy produces a binucleated, dikaryotic (n + n) cell, and the two nuclei then fuse to form a diploid zygote in the step called karyogamy. Meiosis follows to form conidia, which disperse and germinate so that new mycelia form. This exchange of genetic information lets two fungi produce offspring distinct from either parent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Budding is an asexual mode of yeast division and is not part of this sexual sequence.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Germination is the final step in which dispersed conidia form new mycelia, not the step after plasmogamy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Meiosis comes after karyogamy and yields haploid conidia rather than a dikaryotic hypha.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Plasmogamy is the step that already occurred, and it produces a dikaryotic cell rather than a zygote.

questions.stem: A thermally dimorphic fungus takes which of the following forms at 25°C and at 37°C, respectively?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conidium at 25°C and hyphal cyst at 37°C

explanation.summary: Thermally dimorphic fungi are molds at room temperature and budding yeasts at body temperature.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thermally dimorphic fungi are molds at room or ambient temperatures (25°C) and single-celled budding yeasts at human body temperature (37°C). The mnemonic used to remember this is "mold in the cold, yeast in the heat." Histoplasma capsulatum and Blastomyces dermatitidis both display this thermal dimorphism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dimorphism refers to the mold and yeast forms, not to conidia converting into a cyst stage.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A single mold form at both temperatures would mean the organism is not dimorphic at all.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This reverses the relationship; the yeast form appears at body temperature, not at room temperature.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A single yeast form at both temperatures would likewise mean the organism is not thermally dimorphic.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man completes a 10-day course of a broad-spectrum antibiotic for pneumonia. He now reports a sore mouth and a change in taste. Examination shows curd-like white patches on the buccal mucosa and tongue that are easily removed with moderate scraping, leaving an erythematous base. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

explanation.summary: Thrush is an overgrowth of Candida spp. in the mouth, most often after antibiotic use or during immunosuppression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Candida spp. are normal flora of the mouth and throat, and disruption of the normal flora by a broad-spectrum antibiotic allows them to overgrow. Thrush presents as curd-like white patches that are easily removed with moderate scraping. C. albicans is the species responsible for most cases of candidiasis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. exist only as molds and cause lung and sinus disease; they do not produce removable oral plaques.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Epstein-Barr virus causes hairy cell leukoplakia, whose white patches do not come off with scraping.
whyWrongByChoice.D: S. aureus can coinfect angular cheilitis at the corners of the mouth, but it does not cause curd-like removable plaques.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. pyogenes is listed as a cause of cheilitis and diaper rash, not of scrapable white plaques on the tongue.

questions.stem: A student is reviewing the organisms that make up the normal human flora. In healthy people, Candida spp. pose little threat and are recovered as commensals from several body sites. Candida spp. primarily colonize which of the following?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sinuses, middle ear, and lower airways

explanation.summary: Candida spp. are human normal flora of the mouth, throat, gastrointestinal tract, and vagina.
explanation.whyCorrect: Candida spp. live in harmony with most people as normal flora at these mucosal sites. Disease follows immunosuppression or disruption of the normal flora, often from antibiotic use, which allows overgrowth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The urinary tract is not a normal Candida reservoir; Candida cystitis is a hospital-acquired infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blood, liver, and spleen are sterile; Candida spp. reaching the bloodstream represents invasive disease, not colonization.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The sinuses and lower airways are sites Aspergillus spp. can colonize; Candida spp. are not normal flora there.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Soil, decaying vegetation, and air are the environmental reservoirs of Aspergillus spp., not of Candida spp.

questions.stem: A hospital laboratory tabulates every Candida isolate recovered from clinical specimens over one year. A single species accounts for roughly 57 percent of the isolates and is responsible for most cases of candidiasis. Which of the following species is it?

explanation.summary: C. albicans is the single most commonly isolated Candida species and causes the most cases of candidiasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among Candida species isolated in the clinic, C. albicans accounts for about 57 percent, far more than any other species. The remaining isolates are divided among glabrata, parapsilosis, krusei, and tropicalis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: C. glabrata is second at roughly 17 percent of clinical isolates.
whyWrongByChoice.C: C. krusei accounts for roughly 5 percent of clinical isolates.
whyWrongByChoice.D: C. parapsilosis accounts for roughly 8 percent of clinical isolates.
whyWrongByChoice.E: C. tropicalis accounts for roughly 5 percent of clinical isolates.

questions.stem: The same laboratory reports that, after the single most common species, one other species accounts for about 17 percent of clinical Candida isolates, roughly twice the share of the next species on the list. Which species accounts for that 17 percent?

explanation.summary: C. glabrata is the second most frequently isolated Candida species in the clinic at about 17 percent.
explanation.whyCorrect: The relative frequency list runs C. albicans 57 percent, C. glabrata 17 percent, C. parapsilosis 8 percent, then C. krusei and C. tropicalis at 5 percent each. C. glabrata's 17 percent is about twice the 8 percent of C. parapsilosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: C. auris is rarely seen in the United States and does not appear among the common clinical isolates.
whyWrongByChoice.C: C. krusei accounts for roughly 5 percent, not 17 percent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: C. parapsilosis accounts for roughly 8 percent, the species just below the correct answer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: C. tropicalis accounts for roughly 5 percent, tied with C. krusei.

questions.stem: A hospital epidemiologist reviews susceptibility data on Candida auris isolates recovered from intensive care unit patients. Most of the isolates are resistant to fluconazole. Approximately what proportion of C. auris isolates is also resistant to amphotericin B?

explanation.summary: C. auris is commonly multidrug resistant: most isolates resist fluconazole and 13 to 35 percent resist amphotericin B.
explanation.whyCorrect: Between 13 and 35 percent of C. auris isolates are resistant to amphotericin B. Most isolates remain susceptible to the echinocandins, although the minimal inhibitory concentration needed is higher than for C. albicans. Combined with the poor health of the patients it infects, this resistance drives a 30 to 72 percent mortality for hospital-acquired C. auris infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This understates the resistance; amphotericin B resistance in C. auris is common, not exceptional.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is far below the reported range for amphotericin B resistance in this species.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Resistance is substantial but does not reach a majority of isolates.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Near-universal resistance describes fluconazole in this species, not amphotericin B.

questions.stem: An immunocompromised man has white patches on the lateral tongue and buccal mucosa. His physician wants to distinguish oropharyngeal candidiasis from hairy cell leukoplakia at the bedside. Which of the following findings would best support a diagnosis of thrush?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The patches are confined to the lateral border of the tongue

choices.label: B
choices.text: The patches are easily removed with gentle scraping

choices.label: C
choices.text: The patches have been present for many months

choices.label: D
choices.text: The patient also has painful vesicles on the lower lip

choices.label: E
choices.text: The patient reports no recent exposure to antibiotics

explanation.summary: Thrush wipes off with gentle scraping; hairy cell leukoplakia does not.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both thrush and hairy cell leukoplakia present as white oral patches in immunocompromised patients, so they look alike. The quick bedside discriminator is scraping: the curd-like plaques of thrush come off, while the lesions of hairy cell leukoplakia, which is caused by Epstein-Barr virus, remain adherent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Location does not separate the two, and both may involve the tongue and adjacent mucosa.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Duration does not discriminate; both occur in immunocompromised patients and may persist.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lip vesicles are a separate finding and do not distinguish these two white-patch diseases.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antibiotic exposure raises suspicion for thrush, but its absence does not exclude it, since immunosuppression and oral trauma also cause it.

questions.stem: An 81-year-old nursing home resident with no recent antibiotic use and no known immunodeficiency develops white plaques on the gums and palate. Her dentures were fitted many years ago and now slip and rub against her gums when she chews. Which of the following best explains why she developed this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inhaled spores colonized a pre-existing mucosal cavity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Loss of normal flora from a broad-spectrum antibiotic course

choices.label: C
choices.text: Repeated trauma from the ill-fitting dentures damaged her gums

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rising estrogen levels changed her mucosal environment

choices.label: E
choices.text: The infection spread from another resident who shares her denture cup

explanation.summary: Oral trauma, classically from poorly fitting dentures, is a third route to thrush besides antibiotics and immunosuppression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thrush most commonly follows antibiotic use or immunosuppression, but oral trauma can also cause it. Poorly fitting dentures rub against and damage the gums, which can lead to infection by Candida spp. or by the other bacteria in the mouth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Colonization of a pre-existing cavity by inhaled spores describes aspergilloma in the lung, not thrush.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The stem specifies that she has had no recent antibiotic exposure, so loss of flora from antibiotics cannot explain it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increased estrogen is a risk factor for vulvovaginal candidiasis, not for oral thrush.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Candida spp. cause disease by overgrowth of the patient's own normal flora, not by person-to-person spread.

questions.stem: A man with severe immunosuppression is being treated for thrush. He now reports retrosternal chest discomfort and pain with swallowing, and his oral infection is presumed to have extended beyond the mouth. Which of the following complications has most likely developed?

explanation.summary: In severe immunosuppression, thrush can spread beyond the mouth to the pharynx and esophagus, producing Candida esophagitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Esophagitis is one of the five superficial Candida infections and is the direct downstream extension of thrush. Patients with severe immunosuppression are the ones in whom the infection spreads past the oropharynx.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Balanitis is a superficial infection of the penis and is unrelated to extension of oral disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Candida endocarditis follows hematogenous dissemination, not contiguous spread from the mouth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Candida meningitis is a manifestation of disseminated invasive disease in severely ill patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyelonephritis arises from an ascending urinary tract infection, not from oral thrush.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman presents with vulvar itching and a thick, white, curd-like vaginal discharge. She has taken no antibiotics recently, has no history of diabetes, and is not immunosuppressed. Which element of her history is the most likely predisposing factor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She eats a diet that is high in refined sugars

choices.label: B
choices.text: She exercises at a gym three times every week

choices.label: C
choices.text: She recently began combined oral contraceptives

choices.label: D
choices.text: She recently traveled to a hot and humid climate

choices.label: E
choices.text: She uses only unscented laundry soap at home

explanation.summary: Increased estrogen levels, including from birth control, raise the risk of vulvovaginal candidiasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Risk factors for yeast infections are antibiotic use, increased estrogen levels from pregnancy, birth control, or hormone therapy, diabetes, immunosuppression, and anything that alters vaginal pH. The stem excludes antibiotics, diabetes, and immunosuppression, leaving the estrogen exposure from her oral contraceptive.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dietary sugar is not among the listed risk factors for vulvovaginal candidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Routine exercise is not one of the identified predisposing factors for this infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Heat and humidity predispose to Candida intertrigo in skin folds, not to vulvovaginal candidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Using unscented soap does not alter vaginal pH and is not a risk factor.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old uncircumcised man with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes reports several days of burning, tenderness, and itching of the glans and foreskin. Examination shows inflammation with a curd-like exudate beneath the foreskin. Which of the following most likely contributed to his infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A recent course of corticosteroids for an asthma flare

choices.label: B
choices.text: A recent surgical procedure on the genitourinary tract

choices.label: C
choices.text: Failure to retract and clean the prepuce regularly

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prior instrumentation of the urethra with a catheter

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recent sexual contact with a partner who has urethritis

explanation.summary: Candida balanitis is favored by diabetes, obesity, immunosuppression, and being uncircumcised with inadequate hygiene under the foreskin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Failure to clean properly underneath the foreskin leads to overgrowth of normal flora and potentially to infection. Candida balanitis presents with pain, tenderness, burning, and pruritus of the foreskin or penis developing over several days, often with a curd-like or purulent exudate. Having a partner with a vulvovaginal yeast infection also increases risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Corticosteroids are a listed risk for invasive Aspergillus disease, not a described cause of balanitis here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Recent surgery is a risk factor for invasive candidiasis, not for this superficial infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Urethral catheters predispose to urinary tract infection, not to inflammation of the glans and foreskin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A partner with vulvovaginal candidiasis raises risk, but urethritis in a partner is not a listed risk factor for Candida balanitis.

questions.stem: An obese 45-year-old woman has a rash beneath both breasts. The involved skin is red, moist, and shiny, described as beefy in appearance, and several small pustules sit just beyond the border of the main rash. Which combination of local factors best explains this presentation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cold air, wind exposure, and chronic scratching

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contact with detergents, dyes, and added fragrances

choices.label: C
choices.text: Friction, moisture, and heat within the skin folds

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sun exposure, dryness, and repeated shaving of the area

choices.label: E
choices.text: Venous stasis, dependent edema, and poor arterial flow

explanation.summary: Candida intertrigo is inflammation of the skin folds driven by friction, moisture, and heat, with beefy red skin and satellite pustules.
explanation.whyCorrect: Superficial Candida skin infections are often classified as intertrigo, inflammation of the skin folds, and are associated with friction, moisture, and heat. The presentation is described as beefy because the skin is red, moist, and shiny like raw beef, and satellite pustules may be present.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cold and wind do not create the warm, damp fold environment in which Candida spp. overgrow.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Detergents and fragrances produce contact dermatitis, which is not the Candida skin infection described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sun exposure and dryness are the opposite of the moist, occluded environment that favors intertrigo.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Venous stasis and arterial insufficiency cause lower leg skin changes, not fold infection with satellite pustules.

questions.stem: A 9-month-old infant who is finishing a course of amoxicillin for otitis media and recovering from several days of diarrhea develops a rash in the diaper area. The rash consists of beefy red plaques, papules, and pustules that scale when they rupture, and the skin folds are the worst affected. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Diaper rash is often caused by Candida spp., especially after diarrhea, infrequent diaper changes, or recent antibiotics.
explanation.whyCorrect: Candida diaper rash presents as beefy red plaques, papules, and pustules that scale when ruptured, with the skin folds most severely involved. A recent history of diarrhea, infrequent diaper changes, or recent antibiotic use are the commonly associated exposures, and this infant has two of the three.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus spp. are environmental molds causing lung and sinus disease, not diaper dermatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Epstein-Barr virus causes hairy cell leukoplakia in the mouth, not a diaper-area rash.
whyWrongByChoice.D: S. saprophyticus is a cause of urinary tract infection, not of diaper dermatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. pyogenes can cause diaper rash and cheilitis, but the beefy fold-predominant rash following antibiotics and diarrhea points to Candida.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man presents with fever, cough, and myalgias. Two weeks earlier he explored a limestone cave in southern Ohio that was heavily occupied by bats. A chest radiograph shows patchy infiltrates. Which of the following organisms grows especially well in soil enriched with bat and bird droppings?

explanation.summary: Histoplasma spp. live in soil and grow especially well where bird or bat droppings enrich it, so spelunkers are a classic at-risk group.
explanation.whyCorrect: Histoplasma capsulatum is found predominantly in the Ohio and Mississippi river valleys, and its growth is favored by soil enriched with bird or bat droppings. Cave explorers are specifically at increased risk from exposure to bat droppings. Poultry, construction, and landscaping workers are also at elevated risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces spp. grow in soil but have no association with bat or bird droppings; decomposing leaves and wood favor them.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces gilchristii shares the soil habitat of B. dermatitidis and likewise lacks any bat or bird dropping association.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides immitis lives in southwestern desert soil and is not linked to bat guano or to the Ohio river valley.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Coccidioides posadasii also occupies southwestern soil and has no association with bat droppings.

questions.stem: A microbiology instructor asks a student to name the geographically defined fungus that does not convert between a mold form and a yeast form with temperature. Which of the following organisms should the student name?

explanation.summary: Histoplasma, Blastomyces, and Coccidioides spp. are thermally dimorphic; Cryptococcus spp. are yeasts.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cryptococcus spp. are not generally considered dimorphic, although a mold form can be produced under special laboratory conditions. They are described as yeasts in both the environment and patient samples. The other three genera follow the rule 'mold in the cold (25 degrees C), yeast in the heat (37 degrees C).'

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces dermatitidis is thermally dimorphic, with a yeast form recovered from patient samples at 37 degrees C.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coccidioides immitis is thermally dimorphic, converting from arthroconidia-bearing mold to spherules in tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides posadasii is also thermally dimorphic and forms spherules in the host.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Histoplasma capsulatum is thermally dimorphic, growing as a mold at 25 degrees C and a yeast at 37 degrees C.

questions.stem: A sputum sample from a patient with suspected histoplasmosis is inoculated onto Sabouraud agar and incubated at 25 degrees C. Which of the following morphologies is most likely to be recovered from this plate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Encapsulated yeast with an unstained halo

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mold with branching hyphae and conidia

explanation.summary: Thermally dimorphic fungi grow as molds at the cooler incubation temperature of 25 degrees C.
explanation.whyCorrect: The mnemonic for these fungi is 'mold in the cold (25 degrees C), yeast in the heat (37 degrees C).' When Histoplasma spp. are grown at 25 degrees C, they convert to the mold form with hyphae bearing microconidia and macroconidia. Culture on Sabouraud agar can take weeks but confirms the diagnosis and demonstrates thermal dimorphism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An unstained halo around yeast describes the capsule of Cryptococcus spp., which is not thermally dimorphic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Spherules are the tissue form of Coccidioides spp. at body temperature, not a 25 degrees C mold feature.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intracellular yeast within macrophages is the 37 degrees C tissue form of Histoplasma spp., not the culture form.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Broad-based budding yeast is the 37 degrees C form of Blastomyces spp., not a 25 degrees C culture morphology.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man with AIDS who lives in Tennessee has 3 weeks of fever, weight loss, and pancytopenia. A bone marrow aspirate stained with a fungal stain shows numerous 2 to 5 micrometer yeasts with narrow-based budding, many of them inside macrophages. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

explanation.summary: Tiny narrow-based budding yeasts sitting inside macrophages are characteristic of Histoplasma spp.
explanation.whyCorrect: The yeast of Histoplasma spp. are tiny (2 to 5 micrometers) with narrow-based budding, which makes dividing cells look like an hourglass or infinity sign. They are frequently seen inside macrophages and other white blood cells because the organism replicates within macrophages, and dissemination to the bone marrow through the reticuloendothelial system is a recognized feature of severe disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces dermatitidis yeasts are larger than Histoplasma yeasts and show broad-based budding.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coccidioides immitis also forms spherules filled with endospores rather than budding yeasts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides posadasii forms large thick-walled spherules in tissue, not small intracellular budding yeasts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus gattii appears as an encapsulated yeast with a wide unstained zone rather than tiny intracellular forms.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old logger from Wisconsin has a 6-week history of cough and several verrucous skin lesions. A wet preparation of sputum shows large yeasts with a thick connection between the parent and daughter cell. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

explanation.summary: Large yeasts with broad-based budding plus skin lesions point to Blastomyces spp.
explanation.whyCorrect: The yeast of Blastomyces spp. are larger than those of Histoplasma spp. and exhibit broad-based budding, meaning the connection between dividing cells is thick. Skin is the most common site of dissemination in blastomycosis, which fits the verrucous lesions, and outdoor work in an endemic area is the classic exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Coccidioides immitis produces spherules filled with endospores in tissue, not budding yeasts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides posadasii likewise forms spherules in patient samples rather than budding yeast.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus neoformans yeasts are surrounded by a huge capsule and are not described by broad-based budding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Histoplasma yeasts are small with a narrow-based bud, giving an hourglass rather than a thick connection.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman from Tucson, Arizona, has pneumonia that has not improved on azithromycin. A lung biopsy shows a large, round, thick-walled structure packed with small round bodies within the tissue. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

explanation.summary: Spherules filled with endospores are the tissue form unique to Coccidioides spp.
explanation.whyCorrect: After inhaled arthroconidia convert in the host, Coccidioides spp. form giant thick-walled structures called spherules that fill with endospores. The spherule eventually ruptures, releasing endospores into surrounding tissue, and each endospore can form another spherule. Biopsy revealing spherules is diagnostic for coccidioidomycosis, and southern Arizona is a high-incidence area.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces dermatitidis also produces broad-based budding yeast rather than spherules.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces gilchristii produces large broad-based budding yeast, not endospore-filled structures.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus neoformans appears as encapsulated yeast with an unstained zone on staining.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Histoplasma capsulatum appears as tiny narrow-based budding yeast, often inside macrophages.

questions.stem: A mold isolate grown at 25 degrees C from a patient in California's San Joaquin Valley shows hyphae that break up into chains of barrel-shaped cells resembling a bracelet. Which of the following best describes the structures being observed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arthroconidia that fragment from the mycelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Budding yeast with a thick connecting isthmus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Encapsulated yeast with an unstained halo

choices.label: D
choices.text: Endospores released from a ruptured spherule

explanation.summary: Coccidioides spp. make a specialized conidium called an arthroconidium that gives the mold a bracelet-like appearance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Coccidioides spp. have a specialized type of conidia called arthroconidia, which function just like conidia. They break off from the mycelium and allow the fungus to spread, and they give the mold form of Coccidioides spp. a distinct bracelet-like appearance. Inhaled arthroconidia then convert to spherules in the host.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Broad-based budding yeast is the 37 degrees C form of Blastomyces spp.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An unstained halo around yeast describes the capsule of Cryptococcus spp.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Endospores are released inside host tissue when a spherule ruptures, not on a 25 degrees C mold plate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Macroconidia resembling giant suns belong to the mold form of Histoplasma spp.

questions.stem: A fungal isolate incubated at 25 degrees C produces hyphae bearing both very large, distinctly knobby conidia that look like giant suns and much smaller conidia alongside them. Which of the following organisms is most consistent with this mold morphology?

explanation.summary: The mold form of Histoplasma spp. has both microconidia and very distinct macroconidia.
explanation.whyCorrect: When Histoplasma spp. are grown at 25 degrees C they convert to the mold form. Histoplasma spp. have microconidia and macroconidia, and the macroconidia are very distinct, looking like giant suns next to the tinier microconidia. This appearance on culture helps identify the organism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces dermatitidis molds have conidia but no macroconidia, which is precisely how they are distinguished from Histoplasma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coccidioides immitis molds also produce arthroconidia rather than paired micro- and macroconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides posadasii molds make barrel-shaped arthroconidia in a bracelet pattern, not macroconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus gattii is a yeast and is not routinely recovered as a conidia-bearing mold.

questions.stem: A laboratory is examining a mold recovered at 25 degrees C from a patient with pneumonia in an area where both Histoplasma spp. and Blastomyces spp. are endemic. Which of the following culture findings best supports Blastomyces spp. over Histoplasma spp.?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conidia are absent and only bare hyphae are seen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conidia are present but macroconidia are absent

choices.label: D
choices.text: Macroconidia are present and microconidia are absent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thick-walled spherules are present within the hyphae

explanation.summary: Blastomyces molds have conidia but no macroconidia, and that absence separates them from Histoplasma molds.
explanation.whyCorrect: The mold form of Blastomyces spp. has conidia but no macroconidia. The lack of macroconidia distinguishes Blastomyces spp. from Histoplasma spp., whose mold form carries both microconidia and very distinct macroconidia. Because the geographic ranges of the two genera overlap substantially, this morphologic difference is a practical discriminator.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alternating arthroconidia along hyphae is the bracelet appearance of Coccidioides spp.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces molds do produce conidia, so completely bare hyphae would not support the identification.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Macroconidia point toward Histoplasma spp., the organism this finding is meant to exclude.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spherules form in host tissue for Coccidioides spp. and are not a mold culture feature.

questions.stem: A CSF specimen stained with India ink shows round yeast cells each surrounded by a clear, unstained zone against a dark background. Which of the following structures accounts for this unstained zone?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A broad-based bud joining daughter cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: A large polysaccharide capsule around the yeast

choices.label: C
choices.text: A layer of hyphae encircling the yeast

choices.label: D
choices.text: A ring of microconidia around each cell

choices.label: E
choices.text: A thick spherule wall enclosing endospores

explanation.summary: The very large capsule of Cryptococcus spp. excludes stain and produces a clear halo around the yeast.
explanation.whyCorrect: A distinct characteristic of Cryptococcus spp. yeast cells is their very large and distinct capsule. When staining, this huge capsule creates an unstained zone around the yeast. India ink is the classic negative stain method for visualizing the thick capsule of these yeasts in CSF, although it has low sensitivity and is no longer commonly used.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Broad-based budding describes the shape of Blastomyces yeast division, not an unstained zone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptococcus in CSF is a yeast and is not encircled by hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microconidia belong to the mold form of Histoplasma spp. and are not seen around yeast in CSF.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spherules are the tissue form of Coccidioides spp. and do not produce a clear halo on India ink.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man with advanced HIV infection has 2 weeks of headache and confusion. A lumbar puncture is performed and cryptococcosis is suspected. Which of the following is the preferred diagnostic test on this CSF specimen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antigen detection assay on the CSF

choices.label: C
choices.text: India ink negative stain of the CSF

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mucicarmine stain of the CSF sediment

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sabouraud agar culture of the CSF

explanation.summary: Antigen detection assays are the preferred diagnostic test for cryptococcosis in CSF or blood.
explanation.whyCorrect: Several types of antigen detection assays are available to rapidly detect Cryptococcus antigens in CSF or blood, and these antigen detection assays are the preferred diagnostic test. In the brick's case, antigen detection assays of the CNS were performed and Cryptococcus neoformans antigen was detected in a patient with HIV and suspected meningitis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Double immunodiffusion is an antibody assay used for Coccidioides spp., not the preferred cryptococcal test.
whyWrongByChoice.C: India ink is the classic capsule stain but has low sensitivity and is no longer commonly used.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mucicarmine highlights the capsule in red but is used particularly in tissue sections rather than as the preferred test.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Culture is the gold standard for diagnosis but is slower than antigen detection and is not the preferred first test.

questions.stem: Which of the following laboratory methods is considered the gold standard for the diagnosis of cryptococcosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Culture of biopsy, sputum, or blood

choices.label: C
choices.text: India ink stain of a CSF sample

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mucicarmine stain of a tissue section

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum antibody titer against the capsule

explanation.summary: Culture remains the gold standard for diagnosing cryptococcosis, even though antigen assays are preferred for speed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Culture is the gold standard for diagnosis of cryptococcosis. Biopsies, sputum, or blood can be grown on Sabouraud or more specialized agars, and on agar the colonies resemble bacterial colonies. Antigen detection assays are still the preferred diagnostic test in practice because they are rapid.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Double immunodiffusion is an antibody assay applied to coccidioidomycosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: India ink visualizes the capsule but has low sensitivity and is no longer commonly used.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mucicarmine stains the polysaccharide capsule red in tissue sections but is not the gold standard.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antibody titers are not the described method for confirming cryptococcosis in this brick.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man has an intensely itchy, scaly, ring-shaped patch on his forearm. A scraping grows a filamentous fungus that grows readily on dead, keratinized tissue. Which nutrient does this group of fungi prefer, and which secreted enzyme do they use to obtain it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chitin, broken down by secreted chitinase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Collagen, broken down by secreted collagenase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycogen, broken down by secreted amylase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keratin, broken down by secreted keratinase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sebum lipids, broken down by secreted lipase

explanation.summary: Dermatophytes feed on keratin using secreted keratinase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dermatophytes colonize keratinized tissues (skin, hair, and nails). Keratin is a structural protein of those tissues, and dermatophytes secrete keratinase to degrade keratin and use it as an energy source. This is why they stay confined to keratinized structures rather than invading deeper.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chitin is a component of the fungal cell wall itself, the target of calcofluor white stain, not a host nutrient.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Collagen is a dermal protein; dermatophytes do not penetrate into the dermis and do not feed on collagen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glycogen is the fungal cell-wall carbohydrate that PAS stain binds; it is not the nutrient dermatophytes harvest from the host.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lipids are the preferred energy source of Malassezia spp., which is precisely why Malassezia is not classified as a dermatophyte.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman has an itchy, scaly annular rash on her trunk. There is no pus, no fluctuance, and no deep swelling. The infection is confined to the layer of dead, keratinized cells that shields the living epidermis from the environment. Which layer is involved?

explanation.summary: Dermatophyte infections are limited to the stratum corneum, the outermost keratinized layer.
explanation.whyCorrect: The stratum corneum is made of dead, keratinized cells and protects healthy cells from the external environment. Dermatophytes impact only this outermost layer, which is why their infections are itchy and scaly rather than purulent or swollen the way deeper bacterial infections are.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dermatophytes do not penetrate into the dermis; dermal involvement would suggest a different organism such as S. schenckii.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The reticular dermis is deeper still and is unaffected in superficial dermatophyte infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The stratum basale is the deepest, actively dividing epidermal layer and is not colonized by dermatophytes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The stratum spinosum lies deep to the granulosum and lucidum and contains living, non-keratinized cells.

questions.stem: A dermatologist wants to name the one dermatophyte genus that routinely causes disease in all three keratinized sites: skin, hair, and nails. Which genus fits that description?

explanation.summary: Trichophyton spp. cause skin, hair, and nail infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Of the three dermatophyte genera, Trichophyton spp. are the ones described as causing skin, hair, and nail infections. This broad tissue range is why Trichophyton species appear as common causes of tinea corporis, cruris, pedis, barbae, capitis, and unguium.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epidermophyton spp. cause skin and nail infections but not hair infections.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia spp. are not dermatophytes at all; they use lipids and cause pityriasis versicolor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microsporum spp. cause skin and hair infections and only rarely cause nail infections.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sporothrix schenckii is a dimorphic fungus causing subcutaneous, lymphocutaneous disease, not a dermatophyte.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old man has had recurrent tinea cruris and thickened, discolored toenails for years, but has never had scalp or beard involvement. Which dermatophyte genus characteristically infects skin and nails while sparing hair?

explanation.summary: Epidermophyton spp. infect skin and nails, not hair.
explanation.whyCorrect: Epidermophyton spp. are listed as causing skin and nail infections only. Epidermophyton floccosum is among the most common causes of tinea cruris, tinea pedis, tinea corporis, and tinea unguium, but it does not figure among causes of the hair-bearing tineas.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia spp. are lipid-dependent yeasts causing pityriasis versicolor, not nail disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microsporum spp. infect skin and hair and only rarely nails, the opposite of this pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sporothrix schenckii causes ulcerating nodules along lymphatics after skin puncture, not tinea.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trichophyton spp. infect skin, hair, and nails, so hair-bearing sites would not be spared.

questions.stem: A microbiology instructor asks which dermatophyte genus is described as causing skin and hair infections while only rarely infecting nails. Which of the following is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epidermophyton spp., which infect skin and nails

choices.label: B
choices.text: Malassezia spp., which infect sebum-rich skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Microsporum spp., which infect skin and hair

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichophyton spp., which infect skin, hair, nails

explanation.summary: Microsporum spp. cause skin and hair infections and rarely nail infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Microsporum spp. are described as causing skin and hair infections, rarely causing nail infections. This matches their clinical profile: Microsporum canis is a frequent cause of tinea capitis and of tinea corporis among pet owners, but it is not on the list of common onychomycosis pathogens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epidermophyton spp. spare hair entirely, so they do not match a skin-and-hair pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia spp. are not dermatophytes and cause pityriasis versicolor on sebum-rich skin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sporothrix schenckii is not a dermatophyte and spreads along lymphatic channels after inoculation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trichophyton spp. routinely infect nails as well, so nail infection is not rare for them.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old has an expanding lesion on the shoulder with an inflamed, red, scaly advancing border and skin in the center that looks nearly normal. Which mechanism best explains this ring-shaped appearance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Keratinase is secreted only at the leading edge and never within the older central skin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neutrophilic pus accumulates centrally and lifts the infected scale off the skin surface

choices.label: C
choices.text: Scratching mechanically strips the infected stratum corneum away from the lesion center

choices.label: D
choices.text: The fungus exhausts available keratin centrally and then migrates outward to fresh tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: The immune response partially clears the center while the fungus keeps spreading outward

explanation.summary: Central clearing results from the immune system clearing the center while the infection spreads peripherally.
explanation.whyCorrect: As a tinea lesion spreads, the immune system fights the infection and partially clears it in the center while the infection continues to spread outward. The result is centralized clearing with an inflamed, red, scaly advancing border, which is what gives tinea lesions their ring appearance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Keratinase secretion is how dermatophytes feed throughout the lesion; it is not restricted to the border.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dermatophyte infections are characteristically non-purulent; pus suggests bacterial co-infection instead.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Scratching causes breaks in the skin that admit bacteria; it does not create the ring morphology.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Keratin is not depleted; the stratum corneum is continuously renewed and there is no described nutrient-exhaustion mechanism.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old collegiate wrestler has an itchy, red, scaly eruption with an advancing border involving the groin, inner thighs, and scrotum. Which tinea infection does this describe?

explanation.summary: Tinea cruris is jock itch, the dermatophyte infection of the groin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tinea cruris (jock itch) affects the groin and surrounding regions and can involve the thighs, buttocks, and scrotum. It is common in athletes because the thighs rub together during exercise and cause skin damage, increasing the likelihood of infection; tight-fitting clothing contributes for the same reason.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tinea barbae affects the beard area of the face.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tinea corporis is ringworm of the body; it can occur near folds but is not the groin-specific name.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tinea manuum is infection of the hands.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tinea pedis is athlete's foot, affecting the feet, typically starting between the toes.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman has thick, discolored, brittle toenails, and the junction between the nail and the surrounding skin has become disconnected. This infection is also known as onychomycosis. What is the corresponding tinea name?

explanation.summary: Tinea unguium is nail infection, also called onychomycosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tinea unguium is the dermatophyte infection of the nails, also called onychomycosis. It is characterized by thick, discolored nails that may become brittle and break off, and the intersection between the nail and surrounding skin may become disconnected.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tinea barbae affects the beard area.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tinea capitis is scalp infection, most common in children.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tinea corporis is ringworm of the body.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tinea manuum is infection of the hands, not of the nail plate itself.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy has an inflamed, scaly scalp patch with irregular, patchy hair loss. On close inspection the hairs in the affected area are short and stubby and appear as black dots at the scalp surface. Which mechanism explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Comedones form as excess sebum plugs the openings of the hair follicles

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hemorrhage into the hair follicles is caused by vigorous, repeated scratching

choices.label: C
choices.text: Melanin granules are deposited into the follicular openings by the fungus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pigmented fungal colonies grow outward on the surface of the scalp skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: The fungus infects the hair, making it brittle so it breaks before growing out

explanation.summary: Black dots in tinea capitis are hairs made brittle by fungal invasion that break off at the scalp.
explanation.whyCorrect: In tinea capitis, the fungus infects the hair itself, making it brittle so that it breaks off before it can grow out. The residual short, stubby hairs appear as black dots. The associated hair loss is irregular and patchy and is temporary with prompt treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sebum plugging produces comedones, which is a feature of acne rather than dermatophyte infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Scratching can break the skin and admit bacteria but does not produce the black-dot hair pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.C: There is no described fungal deposition of melanin into follicles in tinea capitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The appearance comes from broken hair shafts, not surface colonies of pigmented fungus.

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy has scaly scalp patches with central clearing, an advancing red border, and broken-off hairs. He sleeps with the family dog. A Wood's lamp examination is positive, and a KOH preparation with stain shows microconidia and rough-walled, spindle-shaped macroconidia. Which organism is most likely responsible?

explanation.summary: A pet-associated, Wood's-lamp-positive tinea capitis with spindle-shaped macroconidia is Microsporum canis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Microsporum canis is the dermatophyte that commonly comes from pets, it fluoresces under a Wood's lamp, and Microsporum spp. show rough-walled, spindle-shaped macroconidia with microconidia present. Scalp infections are most frequently caused by Trichophyton and Microsporum species, and tinea capitis is most common in children.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epidermophyton produces smooth, club-shaped macroconidia with no microconidia, and it does not infect hair.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia globosa causes pityriasis versicolor and shows yeast with short hyphae, not macroconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trichophyton spp. show cigar-shaped macroconidia with spiraled hyphae, not spindle-shaped macroconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trichophyton verrucosum is acquired from livestock and is the usual cause of tinea barbae in farmers.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old dairy farmer has itchy, red, crusted lesions in his beard area with patchy loss of beard hair. He handles cattle daily and has no rodent exposure. Which organism is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Trichophyton verrucosum causes livestock-associated tinea barbae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Trichophyton verrucosum causes infections in livestock, and in farmers and others who work with livestock it is the most common cause of tinea barbae. Tinea barbae presents with itchy, red, crusted lesions of the beard area and, like tinea capitis, can cause hair loss in the affected area.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epidermophyton floccosum does not infect hair and so is not a cause of tinea barbae.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Malassezia furfur is a lipid-dependent yeast causing pityriasis versicolor, not beard infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microsporum canis is the pet-associated dermatophyte, typically from dogs and cats rather than cattle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trichophyton mentagrophytes is shed by rodents and is more common in urban environments.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man has itchy, macerated, scaly skin between his fourth and fifth toes. Which clinical form of tinea pedis is this, and how common is it relative to the others?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Interdigital (toe web) form, the least common form

choices.label: B
choices.text: Interdigital (toe web) form, the most common form

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moccasin (chronic hyperkeratotic) form, the most common form

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ulcerative form, the most common form

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vesiculobullous form, the most common form

explanation.summary: The interdigital (toe web) form is the most common presentation of tinea pedis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tinea pedis typically starts between the toes and extends outward. The interdigital, or toe web, form is listed as the most common presentation, predominantly involving the skin between the toes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The site is correctly identified but the frequency is wrong; the interdigital form is the most common.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The moccasin form is a recognized presentation but is not the most common one.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ulceration is a rare complication of tinea pedis, mostly in immunocompromised and diabetic patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The vesiculobullous form produces painful, itchy blisters and is not the most common form.
